title: Tiramisù
intro: Coffee-soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream: Italy's favourite spoon dessert.

steps.t: Make the coffee and let it cool in a shallow bowl.
Separate the eggs: use very fresh ones, as they stay raw. Whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale and foamy.
Add the mascarpone to the yolks a spoonful at a time, stirring until the cream is smooth.
Whisk the whites with the salt to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the cream.
Dip the ladyfingers quickly in the coffee, one at a time, and make a layer in a 20×30 cm dish.
Cover with half the cream, add another layer of dipped ladyfingers and finish with the rest of the cream.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, so it sets.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Just before serving, dust generously with sifted cocoa.

tips.t: One second per side in the coffee is enough: soggy ladyfingers make it watery.
A spoonful of Marsala in the coffee gives it that Italian restaurant flavour.
Covered in the fridge, eat it within 2 days, since the eggs are raw.

title: Panna cotta with berries
intro: Vanilla cream just set, soft and wobbly, with a mixed berry sauce.

steps.t: Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water.
steps.label: Gelatine

steps.t: Meanwhile heat cream, milk, sugar, vanilla seeds and pod until just below the boil.
Take off the heat, remove the pod and stir in the squeezed-out gelatine until dissolved.
Pour the cream into 6 moulds or glasses.
Chill for at least 4 hours, until set but still wobbly.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Cook the berries with the sugar over medium heat until they break down into a sauce.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Dip the moulds in hot water for 5 seconds, turn them out onto plates and spoon over the cold sauce.

tips.t: For a vegetarian version use 2 g agar instead of gelatine and boil it in the cream for 1 minute.
Instead of the berry sauce, try a drizzle of caramel or melted dark chocolate.

title: Crème brûlée
intro: Vanilla custard baked in a water bath under a crust of caramelised sugar.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 150 °C.
Heat the cream with the split vanilla pod and seeds until just below the boil, then turn off the heat.
Leave it to infuse, then remove the pod.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Whisk the yolks with the sugar without beating in air, then slowly pour in the hot cream, stirring.
Strain, skim off the foam and pour into 6 shallow ramekins set in a tray with hot water halfway up.
Bake until the edges are set and the centre barely wobbles.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let them cool, then chill for at least 3 hours.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Sprinkle each with a tablespoon of brown sugar and caramelise it with a blowtorch until amber.

tips.t: No blowtorch? Put the ramekins under the grill on full, very close, for 2 minutes.
Instead of vanilla, infuse the cream with 4 crushed cardamom pods or a strip of orange zest.

title: Chocolate mousse
intro: Just dark chocolate, eggs and a little sugar: light and intense.

steps.t: Melt the chocolate over simmering water, take it off the heat and let it cool until lukewarm.
Separate the eggs, very fresh since they stay raw. Stir the yolks into the chocolate one at a time until thick and glossy.
Whisk the whites with the salt; once foamy add the sugar and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks.
Stir a third of the whites firmly into the chocolate to loosen it.
Fold in the rest gently, lifting from the bottom, until no white streaks remain.
Spoon the mousse into 6 small bowls or one serving dish.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, until set.
steps.label: Chill

tips.t: Use the chocolate lukewarm: hot, it cooks the yolks; cold, it seizes with the whites.
A pinch of flaky salt or chilli on top brings out the cocoa.
Serve with a few raspberries and a spoonful of unsweetened whipped cream.

title: Crema catalana
intro: Milk custard with lemon and cinnamon under a crust of burnt sugar.

steps.t: Heat the milk with strips of lemon peel and the cinnamon until just below the boil.
Turn off the heat, let it infuse, then strain the milk.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Whisk yolks, sugar and cornstarch, pour in the milk slowly, stirring, and return it all to the pan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens and the first bubble appears; take off the heat at once.
steps.label: Custard

steps.t: Pour into shallow terracotta dishes and let it cool.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Just before serving, sprinkle with sugar and burn it with a blowtorch until amber and crisp.

tips.t: Burn the sugar at the last minute: the crust only stays crisp for a few minutes.
In Catalonia it is eaten on Saint Joseph's Day, 19 March: serve it with a small glass of moscatel.

title: Chocolate pudding
intro: Old-fashioned homemade pudding: milk, cocoa and chocolate, no packet mix.

steps.t: In a small saucepan whisk together sugar, cocoa, cornstarch and salt.
Pour in the cold milk slowly, whisking, until there are no lumps.
Bring to the boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, then cook 2 minutes until thick like custard.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Take off the heat and stir in the chopped chocolate until melted.
Pour into a mould rinsed with cold water and left wet, or into 4 small bowls.
Let it cool, cover and chill until firm.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Turn the pudding out onto a plate, or serve it in the bowls.

tips.t: Made with oat or soy milk and dairy-free chocolate it becomes a vegan pudding.
Serve it with a dollop of whipped cream and chopped toasted hazelnuts.

title: Kheer
intro: Indian rice pudding: slowly reduced milk, cardamom, saffron and pistachios.

steps.t: Rinse the rice several times and leave it to soak in cold water.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile bring the milk to the boil in a heavy-based pan.
Add the drained rice and the crushed cardamom seeds, then turn the heat right down.
Simmer, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until the rice breaks down and the milk has reduced and thickened.
steps.label: Kheer

steps.t: Add sugar, saffron and raisins and cook a few minutes more.
steps.label: Sugar

steps.t: Turn off the heat: it thickens as it cools. Serve warm or cold, topped with chopped pistachios and almonds.

tips.t: A teaspoon of rose water stirred in at the end gives it the scent of Diwali sweets.
It thickens a lot when cold: loosen it with a splash of milk before serving.

title: Suspiro a la limeña
intro: Milk caramel cream under a port meringue dusted with cinnamon.

steps.t: In a heavy saucepan, cook both milks over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until they turn into a thick golden manjar.
steps.label: Manjar

steps.t: Beat the yolks, temper them with a ladle of the hot cream, pour back into the pan and cook 2 minutes on low without boiling.
steps.label: Yolks

steps.t: Off the heat, stir in the vanilla, divide among 6 glasses, cool slightly and chill for at least 1 hour.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Meanwhile heat the sugar and port in a small pan to 118 °C, when the syrup falls from a spoon in a thick thread.
steps.label: Syrup

steps.t: Whisk the whites to stiff peaks, pour in the hot syrup in a thin stream while whisking, and keep going until glossy and cool.
steps.label: Meringue

steps.t: Pipe the meringue over the cream with a star nozzle and dust with cinnamon before serving.

tips.t: The manjar is ready when a spatula drawn across the pan leaves the bottom bare for a moment.
No port? A sweet wine such as Marsala works too.
It keeps 2 days in the fridge; the cooked meringue holds its shape.

title: Chè chuối, banana coconut sweet soup
intro: A warm sweet soup of banana, tapioca pearls and coconut, topped with peanuts and sesame.

steps.t: Soak the tapioca pearls in cold water for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile peel the bananas and cut them on the diagonal into 3 cm pieces.
In a saucepan bring the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt to a gentle simmer, stirring.
Add the drained tapioca and cook 8 minutes, stirring often, until the pearls turn clear.
steps.label: Tapioca

steps.t: Add the bananas and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until soft but still whole.
steps.label: Bananas

steps.t: Serve warm in bowls, topped with chopped peanuts and toasted sesame.

tips.t: With the small bananas from Asian shops (chuối sứ) it's more fragrant and the pieces hold their shape.
It's good cold too; it thickens in the fridge, so loosen it with a splash of water.

title: Tangyuan, black sesame rice balls
intro: Soft, chewy glutinous rice balls with a molten black sesame centre.

steps.t: Toast the sesame in a dry pan over low heat, stirring, until it crackles and smells nutty.
steps.label: Sesame

steps.t: Grind it finely with the sugar in a mortar or spice grinder, then work in the lard to a thick paste.
Chill the filling until firm.
steps.label: Fridge

steps.t: Meanwhile add the water to the flour a little at a time and knead to a smooth dough like modelling clay, soft but not sticky.
Roll 20 balls of filling and 20 of dough. Flatten each piece of dough into a cup, add the filling, seal and roll smooth in your palms.
Drop them into plenty of boiling water and stir gently. Once they float, cook for 2-3 minutes more.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Serve 5 each in small bowls with a little of the hot cooking water. Careful: the filling is scalding.

tips.t: Use coconut oil instead of lard and the dessert is vegan.
In China they're also served in a sweet ginger syrup, lovely in winter.
Freeze them uncooked on a floured tray, then boil from frozen for 2 extra minutes.

title: Gulab jamun
intro: Milk dough balls fried slowly and left to swell in a cardamom and rose syrup.

steps.t: Bring the sugar, water, crushed cardamom and saffron to the boil in a small pan, then simmer until just slightly sticky.
steps.label: Syrup

steps.t: Take off the heat, stir in the rose water and keep the syrup warm.
In a bowl mix the milk powder, flour and baking soda, then rub in the ghee with your fingertips.
Add the milk a spoonful at a time and mix without overworking into a soft dough. Cover and let it rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Grease your hands and roll about 20 smooth 2.5 cm balls with no cracks.
Heat the oil to 140 °C and fry the balls over low heat, swirling the oil, until evenly dark brown.
steps.label: Fry

steps.t: Drain and drop them, still hot, into the warm syrup. Let them soak and swell for at least 1 hour.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Serve warm or at room temperature with a little syrup and chopped pistachios.

tips.t: If the oil is too hot they darken outside and stay raw inside: they need to cook slowly and puff up.
Warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, they're a classic Indian festive dessert.
They keep 4 days in the fridge in their syrup: warm for 20 seconds in the microwave.

title: Arroz con leche, Spanish rice pudding
intro: Rice simmered slowly in milk with lemon peel and cinnamon, creamy and fragrant.

steps.t: Heat the milk with strips of lemon peel, no white pith, and the cinnamon stick until it's about to boil.
steps.label: Milk

steps.t: Add the unwashed rice and salt; cook over low heat, stirring often, until creamy and the grains are very soft.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Remove the peel and cinnamon, add the sugar and cook a little longer, stirring: it thickens as it cools.
steps.label: Sugar

steps.t: Spoon into bowls and let it cool to warm, or chill it if you prefer it cold.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Dust with ground cinnamon just before serving.

tips.t: Don't rinse the rice and add the sugar only at the end: the starch makes it creamy and the grains soften fully.
Asturian style: cover with sugar and caramelize it with a blowtorch into a crisp crust.
It keeps 3 days in the fridge: if it gets too thick, stir in a splash of milk.

title: Banana pudding
intro: Layers of vanilla custard, bananas and softened wafers: the South's best-loved pudding.

steps.t: In a saucepan, whisk the sugar, cornstarch and salt, then the yolks, and finally the milk in a thin stream.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until the custard thickens and starts to bubble; then 1 minute more.
steps.label: Custard

steps.t: Off the heat, stir in the butter and vanilla, press cling film onto the surface and let it cool.
steps.label: Cooling

steps.t: Whip the cream with the powdered sugar to soft peaks and slice the bananas.
In a dish, layer wafers, bananas and custard; repeat, finishing with custard.
Spread the whipped cream on top and crumble over a few wafers.
Chill for at least 4 hours: the wafers soften until they are almost like sponge cake.
steps.label: Chill

tips.t: The originals are American vanilla wafers from US food shops; plain butter biscuits work too.
The old-school Southern way: top with a meringue of 3 egg whites and 80 g sugar, browned at 200 °C for 5 minutes.
It keeps for 2 days covered in the fridge; the bananas darken a little but it still tastes great.
